Aims and Values
‘Everyone has the right to be happy’. We take happiness so seriously we made it the first of our school rules! For us it’s crucial and we believe good things flow from it.
Aims
Values
There are six core character values which we expressly want to develop.
At Bancroft’s Prep we do not believe in encumbering children with too many rules and sanctions but focus instead on positive behaviour and rewards.
Our headline ‘3 ½ School Rules’ reinforce our ethos:
Ultimately, we believe it is our role to bring out the very best in our children. We want to help prepare them for the world beyond school where the ability to lead a happy life is as important as the ability to read or reckon. We want our children to have fun while they learn and to derive a lifelong love of learning.
Everyone has the right to be happy.
Respect other people and their property.
Use your common sense.
If in doubt, ask.

Welcome from Mr Layburn
We have a rich and varied curriculum and we keep it that way throughout the four years the children are with us. The guaranteed transfer from the Prep to our Senior School means we don’t need to narrow everything down to focus on an entrance test at 11+ but we do ensure that the children are extremely well prepared for all the academic challenges they will go on to face.
Ours is a vibrant school which benefits from contemporary buildings and impressive shared facilities within the Bancroft’s campus. The Prep children enjoy the freedom that comes from having plenty of space in which to play within a beautifully landscaped and secure site. Whilst they are with us, we aim to give every child a breadth and depth of experience in the academic, cultural and sporting aspects of school life that will stay with them for the years to come.
There is a buzz about the Prep, not least because the children are clearly having fun whilst they learn. We have a very talented and committed staff who enjoy working in our diverse and harmonious school community.
I very much hope that you will consider Bancroft’s as a school for your child; it is a place that can set them up for life.

Welcome
At home on a magnificent greenfield site in Woodford since 1889, but still connected to inner London by the Central Line and our own bus network, we remain committed to welcoming girls and boys from a wide range of backgrounds to enjoy an excellent education as members of our warm, vibrant and supportive Bancroft’s School community.
We are proudly devoted to scholarship and intellectual inquiry, and we believe that each child will truly flourish by combining academic endeavour with enthusiastic engagement in the wide range of co-curricular opportunities that we provide, while being supported and nurtured by our first-class pastoral care.
As an inclusive, cosmopolitan community, we hold the highest aspirations for every young person who joins us.
Our aim is for all Bancroftians to enjoy and make the most of their time at school, while developing the independence of mind and lasting confidence that will empower them to thrive in their future studies and adult lives.
If you might be interested in finding out more about what a Bancroft’s education could offer your son or daughter, we would be delighted to meet you. Please get in touch – you will be assured of a warm welcome.
Alex Frazer MA (Cantab) Head
“The school provides a broad and ambitious curriculum that prioritises both academic achievement and pupils’ wellbeing.”

Spiritual Life
Our ethos is one of mutual respect and acceptance of those from all traditions and backgrounds. The Chapel plays a central role in promoting this ethos and in providing inclusive acts of worship. Chapel services focus on shared values and common concerns, encouraging pupils to reflect on questions of meaning and purpose, and helping them to develop spiritually and morally.
“Pupils develop their spiritual understanding through reflection and discussion.”
There are also opportunities for those from particular faiths to meet together. These currently include regular Communion Services, meetings of the Christian Union, Jewish Society, Muslim Society, and Hindu Society, as well as weekly Muslim assemblies. These gatherings provide space for pupils to share and develop their individual faiths within a community that celebrates difference and shared values alike.
Meet our Chaplain
Our Chaplain, Reverend Simon Richardson, brings warmth, curiosity, and a deep commitment to interfaith understanding.

Sixth Form at Bancroft’s is a place where ambition meets opportunity. It’s two years of challenge and discovery that prepare you not only for A Levels, but for university, careers and life beyond school. The Drapers' Company
The Art of Giving
More than six centuries ago a group of merchants came together to promote their trade in woollen cloth in the City of London. As their guild and fellowship grew, they made philanthropy part of the plan.
Today, the Drapers’ Company has evolved from a trade association into a grant-giving body. We are still a fellowship but now we attract people from all trades and professions, people who find delight, purpose and companionship in serving others. Our members join us to help causes they believe in, to share their expertise, and to build on centuries of experience of the art of giving.
We look after trusts left in our care and manage our investments so that we can confidently make long-term commitments to our charity partners.
Essential human need – the provision of food, clothes, shelter, education and hope – is always our priority.
Welcome to the Drapers’ Company. We have a long history but are as active and relevant today as ever. Our work spans education and philanthropy and the website illustrates many of the ways we make a difference. Since the 16th century we have championed education, now supporting over 30 schools, universities, colleges and conservatoires, with many Drapers’ acting as governors and mentors. We also support ex-offenders, the homeless, ex-service personnel and others in need, as well as caring for residents living in our Almshouses. We are proud of the affiliations we have with the Armed Forces and British Transport Police. Nothing we do would be possible without the dedication of fellow members of the Company and the team at Drapers’ Hall. I am very grateful for all they do to ensure we remain ‘An Enduring Force for Good’. I hope you enjoy this website and seeing how our history and members inspire our actions today.
Master of the Drapers’ Company, 2025-26

Governors
Appointed by the Drapers’ Company
Mr L Savage (Chair of Governors) BEng (Hons), ACGI, FCA, FQMUL
Recognising the importance that his Drapers’ funded education at Bancroft’s had played in his life, Luke joined the Drapers’ Company in 2013 in order to have the opportunity to “give something back”. Luke serves on the Investment Committee, as a Court Assistant and, for 8 years, was one of the Drapers’ Council Members and Treasurer at Queen Mary University London.
Luke is married to Diana and they have two grown up children. He splits his time between London and Bosham (on Chichester Harbour) where he enjoys his keen interest in sailing.
Mr R Sankey BSc (Hons), MBA
Richard’s current role is Client Investment Director at CCLA, working predominantly with charities, endowments and public sector investors. He is a trustee of the Forces Employment Charity (originally The Officers’ Association) and previously sat on the investment committee of the Drapers’ Company which he has been a member of since 1991.
He is married with two daughters and in his spare time enjoys playing golf, sailing and skiing as well as competing in the occasional triathlon.
In his role as a Governor of Bancroft’s Family of Schools, Richard is Chair of our Finance Committee.
Mr R van Maanen BSc, FRICS, ACIArb, ACIOB
Richard attended Bancroft’s between 1972-1979. Having been admitted into the Drapers’ Company, he was appointed as a Governor in 2018.
He is married to Susan and they have two children and live in Woodford Green. He enjoys sport, music, art and messing around with old cars.
In his role as a Governor of Bancroft’s Family of Schools, Richard is Chair of our Estates Committee and is our Welfare, Health and Safety link Governor.
Co-Opted
Mr D Abbot LLB, ACA
Duncan moved to the area when training as a chartered accountant with PwC having read law at Manchester. He has worked in financial services in the City for most of his career. He was, until recently, a Fellow of the Chartered Institute for Securities & Investment. He has sat on the board of public and private companies.
He has lived in Loughton with his wife Gail for 35 years.
In his role as a Governor of Bancroft’s Family of Schools, Duncan is Chair of our Foundation Committee.
Ms T Ashaye
She holds a degree in Financial Economics, a Master’s in Management of Information Technology, and has over 25 years experience in technology across multiple industries, including roles at global organisations such as Apple and Disney.
Tolani is passionate about promoting diversity in STEM and volunteers with organisations including STEM Ambassadors and Career Ready to support young people in education and employment pathways.
She previously served on the Governing Body of Woodford Green Preparatory School and brings this experience, alongside her professional background, to her role in supporting the school.
As a Governor of Bancroft’s Family of School’s, Tolani is a member of our Full Governing Board.
Mrs Debra Davidson-Smith MA, BA
Following her highly successful media career, she now serves as a Magistrate at the East London Family Court and on the North East London bench for criminal matters and carries out work for the History of Parliament Trust Oral History Project.
An alumna of Woodford County High School, Debra has a BA in History from the University of Warwick and a postgraduate diploma in Journalism. Returning to university as a mature student, she completed an MA in History from Queen Mary University and has since had her historical research published in ‘History Today’.
Debra sings with Barts Choir, one of London’s largest professionally rehearsed choral societies. She lives in Buckhurst Hill with her husband Duncan and has two sons.
As a Governor of Bancroft’s Family of School’s, Debra is a member of our Full Governing Board.
Mrs N Dawson BA
Her pastoral interests include character education and bereavement, alongside a broad commitment to safeguarding. Nicky believes that safe and secure students are happy students, and that happy students will thrive. She also feels strongly that education should not only ensure academic success but help young people become well-rounded individuals who are fully prepared to engage with, and contribute to, the world around them.
Nicky is married with two young children.
As a Governor of Bancroft’s Family School of Schools, Nicky is a member of our Full Governing Board and is Safeguarding Governor for Bancroft’s School.
Mr Michael Foster AA Dipl, MA, RIBA
Michael was Secretary of The Standing Conference of Heads of Schools of Architecture (SCHOSA) and President of The Architectural Association. He also edited the book ‘The Principles of Architecture: Style, Structure and Design’. He is currently a Trustee of the Charles S French Charitable Trust and was responsible for the design of recent new buildings projects at St Aubyn’s School where he was a pupil and a recent Governor and Chairman (2021-2024).
Michael graduated from The Architectural Association School of Architecture and he also has an MA in the The History and Theory of Architecture from the University of Essex.
As a Governor of Bancroft’s Family of School’s, Michael is a member of our Full Governing Board.
Mrs C Jones LLB (Hons)
Having taken a career break to bring up her children, Claire worked as Clerk to the Governors at Chigwell School and was a Governor at Woodford County High School for 17 years.
Claire lives in Woodford and both her children attended Bancroft’s School from the Alphas in the Prep through to the Sixth Form.
As a Governor of Bancroft’s Family of Schools, Claire is Chair of our Prep Committee.
Mr R Kalia
He has been a resident of South Woodford since childhood and attended a small, independent primary school before moving on to Ilford County High School, and later studied law at Queen Mary and Westfield College, University of London.
Rajesh lives in South Woodford with his wife and has a son and daughter. One is currently attending university, while the other attends Bancroft’s. Through St Aubyn’s and Bancroft’s, he has enjoyed an association of more than 25 years with the schools. He has served as a Governor at St Aubyn’s since 2018, most recently as Chair. In his spare time, Rajesh is a keen football enthusiast and a season ticket holder at West Ham.
As a Governor of Bancroft’s Family of School’s, Rajesh is a member of our Full Governing Board.
Dr K Satchithananda BDS, FDCRSC, MBBS, FRCS, FRCR
Keshthra sits on the National Clinical Advisory Group for National Breast Screening and is the chair of the National Radiology Clinical Professional Group for NHS England. These inform and advise the Department of Health and NHSE on guidance and policy.
She is married with two sons who attended Bancroft’s school until 2020.
In her role as a Governor of Bancroft’s Family of Schools, Keshthra is Chair of our Education Committee.
Mrs J Venditti
Justine began her career in Materials Engineering before retraining as a Mathematics teacher. She rapidly progressed into leadership, bringing a strong analytical approach and a clear commitment to educational excellence. Her work spans curriculum innovation, staff development, and whole-school improvement, with a particular interest in creating ambitious, inclusive learning environments. She has extensive experience in policy development and regulatory compliance within the independent sector. Through her work, she combines strategic oversight with a strong focus on people – supporting staff, engaging with parents, and ensuring that every pupil is able to thrive.
Justine is married with two grown up children.
As a Governor of Bancroft’s Family of School’s, Justine is a member of our Full Governing Board and is Safeguarding Governor for St Aubyn’s School and Woodford Green Prep School.

The Arts Society
The Arts Society, Woodford Green (Bancroft’s)
The Arts Society Essex Website
The Arts Society, Woodford Green (Bancroft’s) (previously BADFAS) was formed as an independent charity in 1979 by members of the local community and members of the School’s Senior Management Team. It is a member group of The Arts Society – a nationwide organisation of more than 330 local societies and over 90,000 members with a mutual interest in the decorative arts.
The Arts Society, Woodford Green continues to enjoy a close association with the School. The Head is our President and we meet in the Prep School Hall. We also make annual contributions toward the music tuition fees of promising musicians from the School.
Our aims are to promote an interest in and increased knowledge of decorative and fine arts. We enjoy lectures from well-qualified speakers on a variety of art and art history subjects and we occasionally hold study days to explore a subject in greater depth. In parallel with this programme, we have a programme of visits and an annual five day ‘holiday’. Lectures are held on the second Tuesday of the month during term time, lectures commence at 8pm with coffee and wine available from 7.30 pm.
For details of how to join us, please email our Membership Secretary, Elaine Malone at:
artssocietywoodfordgreen@outlook.com

Drama
Beyond the classroom, our productions bring together energy, creativity and collaboration. Recent senior shows have included Captain Corelli’s Mandolin, We Will Rock You and School of Rock, while Brilliant the Dinosaur and Bye Bye Birdie have delighted younger audiences. Each production showcases the ambition and imagination of our pupils, supported by a dedicated Theatre Technician and a team of staff who help bring each performance to life.
There are plenty of ways to get involved beyond the main stage, from the Inter-House Performing Arts Competition and Junior Drama Club to Taal, our multicultural performance society. Pupils can also explore technical theatre, stage management and design.
Bancroftians have regularly performed at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival, earning praise for their bold and original productions. Theatre trips and professional workshops run by visiting actors and directors offer inspiration throughout the year.
We are fortunate to have two performance spaces: the traditional Great Hall and the flexible Performing Arts Centre, both equipped with modern sound and lighting systems. Together they ensure that Drama at Bancroft’s continues to thrive – challenging, creative and full of life.
Diverse Opportunities
Students can participate in various aspects of drama, from acting to technical roles such as sound and lighting design. Our dedicated technician is delighted to work with anyone interested in learning more about these areas. We also welcome those who want to help with sourcing and building sets and props for our productions.

Music
Beyond the classroom, there is a rich co-curricular programme of orchestras, choirs, bands and smaller ensembles. Many pupils also form their own groups, performing popular music and exploring new styles together.
“As a musician who enjoys playing many genres, it’s amazing to have the chance to explore such a variety of music.”
The Music Department is based in the Stave, which includes a large rehearsal space, teaching rooms, practice rooms and a technology suite equipped with Apple Macs for recording and composition. Instrumental and vocal tuition is available each week from a team of experienced visiting staff, and pupils benefit from regular masterclasses with professional musicians.
Concerts take place throughout the year, both in school and at venues in the local area and in London. The highlight of the musical calendar is the annual concert at Drapers’ Hall in the City of London. Every group performs at least once a year, and there are regular opportunities for soloists. House music events, organised largely by senior pupils, add to the vibrancy of musical life, from assemblies and family evenings to the annual Inter-House Performing Arts Competition.

Frequently Asked Questions
What is Bancroft’s School?
Bancroft’s is a fully co-educational independent day school for children aged 7 to 18, located on the north-east London/Essex border.
What age groups and entry points does Bancroft’s offer?
Bancroft’s educates pupils from 7–18, with key entry points at 7+ (Year 3), 11+ (Year 7) and 16+ (Sixth Form).
Read more about each stage in the admissions journeys for 7+ entry, 11+ entry and 16+ entry.
How do admissions work?
Our admissions process varies by entry point and year group. See the 7+ admissions page, the 11+ admissions page and the 16+ admissions page for more information.
You can also find out more about Occasional Places.
Do prep school pupils need to sit the 11+ to move up to senior school?
No. Every pupil at Bancroft’s Prep automatically progresses to the Senior School, and this guaranteed continuity is one of the most significant advantages of joining the school at 7+.
Can we visit the school?
Yes, we would be delighted to welcome you. Visiting is the best way to understand day-to-day life at Bancroft’s.
See upcoming open events and tours on the Visit Us page.
Where can I register my interest or apply?
You can register online for the relevant entry point via Register Online.
What does the curriculum look like?
Pupils follow a structured academic journey supported by enrichment and co-curricular opportunities.
Explore the Senior School curriculum (11–16) and the Sixth Form curriculum.
Do you offer bursaries or scholarships?
Yes. Bancroft’s offers bursaries (means-tested financial support) and scholarships/awards (including academic merit awards for Senior School entry).
Read more about Bursaries and Scholarships and Awards.
Where is Bancroft’s located?
The school is based in Woodford Green on the north-east London/Essex border. Full address and details are on the Contact page.
Does Bancroft’s have a school bus?
Yes. Find out more about routes, drop-off and pick-up locations, and ticket options on the School Bus Service page.
How do I contact the school?
For all enquiries, including Admissions, please use the details on our Contact page.
What public transport links serve the school?
Bancroft’s is well served by public transport, making it easy to get to without a car. The school is in Woodford Green, close to London Underground and several bus routes.
Tube: The Central line serves nearby stations including South Woodford and Woodford.
Buses: Several London bus routes stop close to the school, including 179, 20, 397, 657, and 679.
What are the West Grove sports facilities, and where are they?
Bancroft’s West Grove Playing Fields are the school’s off-site sports grounds in Woodford Green.
Address: West Grove Playing Fields, Ray Lodge Road, Woodford Green, Essex, IG8 7NZ.
West Grove includes a range of outdoor facilities used for games and fixtures, including tennis and netball courts, cricket, football, and rugby pitches, a CrossFit gym, and cricket nets. It is also used for athletics, including the school’s grass track at West Grove.
